main.headline: OpenAI to acquire developer tooling startup Pierre Computer
main.summary: OpenAI announced plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company, which runs a cloud code-storage service and builds open-source libraries. Two of them, Trees and Diffs, already power the interface of OpenAI's Codex coding tool. OpenAI says the deal is meant to improve Git workflows when developers and AI agents write code together, and it will keep Pierre's open-source projects open. Terms were not disclosed, and The Decoder reports the deal still needs regulatory approval.

main.headline: Voters approve about two dozen data center restrictions in midterms
main.summary: Of 41 data center measures on ballots across 10 states, about two dozen that restrict or block development appeared to pass, according to Ballotpedia via Axios. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor's race after campaigning for a data center construction moratorium until the state passes new legislation. Texas accounts for 41% of new US data center capacity in 2028, according to SemiAnalysis. In NBC News and SSRS exit polls, 56% of respondents called AI and data centers a decisive or important factor, the lowest of five topics surveyed.

main.headline: US tech stocks recover as Nasdaq gains 0.83% on election day
main.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.37% and the Nasdaq 0.83% on Tuesday, according to The Guardian, ending a selloff in AI and tech shares. Nvidia gained 2.3%, and the Dow fell 0.38% after Apple dropped 1.9% on a margin forecast. The Guardian reports the elections had little visible effect on Wall Street, though investors expect Democrats to gain House control, which could mean more AI regulation. Other outlets report mixed moves: Yahoo Finance says Microsoft rose while Tesla and Nvidia fell.
